title: Adaptive microblock reclamation and decode pacing to stabilize tail latency for paged KV cache
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Under mixed workloads, paged KV caches exhibit tail latency spikes when prefill activity and decode waves coincide with reclamation of small fragmented microblocks. Existing LRU-style eviction and aggressive compaction cause jitter for tenants with bursty long-context requests.

Goal: Implement an adaptive microblock reclamation policy paired with decode pacing heuristics and kernel-selection hints that: (1) reduces 99th/99.9th percentile decode latency, (2) clarifies tenant-level interference boundaries, and (3) bounds CPU/GPU reclamation overhead during prefill.

Scope: Changes primarily within the paged-attention KV manager and the prefill coordinator. Work items include: microblock aging buckets, low-overhead fragmentation sampler, opportunistic compaction windows, tenant-weighted reclaim throttles, decode pacing tokens that cooperatively yield to high-priority latency-critical RPCs, and a compact kernel-hint header that guides the runtime's kernel selector to prefer low-latency kernels for imminent decode waves.
acceptance_criteria: P99 decode latency improvement >= 25% on mixed production-like trace compared to baseline run
P99.9 decode latency regression <= 5% for latency-critical tenant under peak load
End-to-end increase in extra GPU reclamation cycles < 8% compared to baseline
No regression in throughput for bulk batch workloads (>5% tolerance)
Feature gated with runtime flag and covered by integration test harness (replay + chaos)
work_items: Design: define microblock metadata (last-touch, frag-score, tenant-weight)
Runtime: implement age-bucketed microblock scanner with probabilistic sampling
Prefill coordinator: add decode pacing token bucket and priority preemption path
Kernel-selector: add low-latency hint header and fallback scoring adjustment
Tests: synthetic mixed-workload benchmark and CI replay of production trace
Docs: Console description of 'Reclaim pressure' metric and per-tenant knobs
progress_updates: 2026-02-14: Kickoff meeting — scoped to paged-attention KV manager and prefill coordinator. Agreed to preserve current API surface and feature-flag rollout.
2026-02-22: Prototype microblock sampler in experiment branch (perf/kv/micro-sample). Early sampling shows 30% fewer compactions when using frag-score threshold 0.35.
2026-03-01: Added decode pacing token bucket; integrated with request priority metadata. Local perf: P99 improved by ~18% on 90/10 mixed trace.

2026-03-05: Design review with runtime team — decision to expose kernel low-latency hint as ephemeral header to avoid persistent model artifacts. Runtime agreed to accept hint with a bounded penalty if kernel unavail.
2026-03-09: Running long replay on canary; observed one tenant isolation gap during concurrent long-context prefill; investigating spillover thresholds and per-tenant soft-quota enforcement.
decisions: Use probabilistic sampling for fragmentation detection instead of full scan to limit CPU overhead (decided 2026-02-22).
Implement tenant-weighted reclaim budgets to prevent a single noisy tenant triggering global compaction (decided 2026-03-01).
Expose kernel hint as non-authoritative preference; runtime may ignore if incompatible with scheduled kernel (decided 2026-03-05).
risks: Incorrect frag-score calibration could either over-compact (wasting cycles) or under-compact (leaving fragmentation that increases evictions).
Decode pacing interacts with autoscaler burst windows — risk of underutilization if tokens are too conservative.
Kernel hint adds complexity to selection logic; poorly chosen mapping may increase tail latency for other workloads.
mitigations: Start with conservative thresholds and alpha-tune using production replay; add per-tenant canary before global rollout.
Measure autoscaler metrics in canary and coordinate with capacity team to allow short burst credits during trials.
Add telemetry to collect kernel-hint accepts/ignores and correlate with observed latency; provide fast rollback feature-flag.
notes: Alternate approach considered: global background compactor that runs at low priority. Rejected due to interference with prefill windows (see 2026-02-20 notes).
Bench harness: use production trace replay (2026-01) with synthetic tenant spikes to evaluate worst-case isolation.
Cross-team: coordinate with Dedicated autoscaling team to ensure reclaim-induced throttles don't count as failures for SLA calculators.
qa_plan: Unit tests for frag-score calculation and sampler determinism
Integration replay: three traces (steady, bursty, mixed) with baseline vs feature-flag runs
Chaos test: inject sudden tenant long-context spike while running compaction to validate isolation
